entities.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
Istituto per le Opere di Religione (IOR)
Administration of the Patrimony of the Apostolic See (APSA)
The Theosophical Society in England (2015 incorporated company)
entities.reason: Separate national legal body identified in BIN-S08; do not merge with 1875/1905 Adyar identity.

sources.title: How is the Federal Reserve System structured?
sources.sourceLocator: FAQ body, paragraphs 1–4; rendered lines 9–13; date is Last Update
sources.passageSummary: The official account distinguishes Board, FOMC and 12 Reserve Banks. It identifies the Board as a federal agency accountable to Congress, overseeing the Reserve Banks.
sources.limits: Bounded published passage only; no full archive, account, transaction or independent performance audit.

sources.title: Who owns the Federal Reserve?
sources.sourceLocator: FAQ body, rendered lines 10–16; date is Last Update
sources.passageSummary: The FAQ distinguishes the System from separately incorporated Reserve Banks and describes member-bank stock as a statutory membership requirement unlike ordinary corporate stock.
sources.limits: Bounded published passage only; no full archive, account, transaction or independent performance audit.

sources.title: About the Bank for International Settlements
sources.sourceLocator: Mission paragraph and four bullets, rendered lines 509–515
sources.passageSummary: BIS describes its mission as supporting central banks through cooperation and providing a forum, analysis, knowledge-sharing and banking services.
sources.limits: Bounded published passage only; no full archive, account, transaction or independent performance audit.

sources.title: Mission and Vision
sources.publisher: Istituto per le Opere di Religione
sources.sourceLocator: Mission section, rendered lines 188–194, citing Statutes art. 2
sources.passageSummary: IOR describes custody and administration of entrusted or transferred property intended for religious or charitable purposes. Its ethical aspirations are self-description, not a completed conduct audit.
sources.independenceRoot: Istituto per le Opere di Religione
sources.limits: Bounded published passage only; no full archive, account, transaction or independent performance audit.

sources.title: Praedicate Evangelium — APSA
sources.passageSummary: The constitution assigns APSA administration of specified assets and services for the Curia; art. 219 §3 says execution of the transactions specified in §§1–2 takes place through IOR. These are distinct named institutions with a stated functional connection.
sources.limits: Bounded published passage only; no full archive, account, transaction or independent performance audit.

sources.title: Mission, Objects and Freedom statements
sources.sourceLocator: Three Objects / Freedom of Thought; rendered lines 7–16
sources.passageSummary: The institution dates formation to 17 November 1875 and Madras incorporation to 3 April 1905; its objects concern universal brotherhood, comparative study and unexplained nature/human capacities. Its stated 1924 resolution permits members to reject doctrines.
sources.limits: Bounded published passage only; no full archive, account, transaction or independent performance audit.

sources.title: Early History
sources.sourceLocator: The Society is Founded; rendered lines 15–17
sources.passageSummary: The institutional retrospective connects a September 1875 lecture on Egyptian proportions with the formation decision and dates Olcott’s inaugural address to 17 November 1875. Its spiritual claims remain attributed institutional narration.
sources.limits: Bounded published passage only; no full archive, account, transaction or independent performance audit.

sources.title: Charity registration decision: The Theosophical Society in England
sources.publisher: Charity Commission for England and Wales
sources.sourceLocator: Background / Decision / What are the purposes; rendered lines 84–105
sources.passageSummary: The decision dated 20 June 2016 accepts charitable status for the English body on education and moral/ethical improvement grounds; it describes the company incorporated 28 July 2015 as successor to an unincorporated organization.
sources.independenceRoot: Charity Commission for England and Wales
sources.limits: Bounded published passage only; no full archive, account, transaction or independent performance audit.
